st: Put the beef, water, bay leaves and [[1 tsp]] salt in a large pot. Bring to a boil and skim off the foam.
Lower the heat and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes until the beef is tender. Remove the beef, shred the meat, and discard the bones.
Heat the oil in a skillet. Cook the onion and carrots for 6 minutes.
Add the beets, tomato paste and vinegar to the skillet. Cook 8 minutes, stirring, until the beets soften.
Add the potatoes to the broth and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the cabbage and the beet mixture. Simmer for 15 minutes until everything is tender.
Return the beef to the pot with the garlic, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Simmer 5 more minutes.
Let the soup stand for 15 minutes. Ladle into bowls and top with sour cream and dill.
Mix the flour, egg, [[1 tsp]] salt and warm water. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Rest covered for [[30 minutes]].
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes until soft. Drain well and mash.
Cook the onions in [[2 tbsp]] butter for 10 minutes until golden. Stir half into the potatoes with the cheese, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper.
Roll the dough thin and cut out 3-inch circles with a glass.
Put a spoonful of filling in each circle. Fold over and pinch the edges tightly to seal.
Boil the varenyky in salted water in batches. They are done 3 minutes after they float.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and toss in [[2 tbsp]] butter.
Serve with the remaining fried onions and sour cream.
Boil the cabbage head in a large pot for 10 minutes. Peel off the soft leaves, and trim thick ribs.
Simmer the rice in water for 8 minutes, drain, and cool.
Cook half the onion and the carrots in oil for 8 minutes.
Mix the pork, rice, remaining raw onion, [[1 tsp]] salt, pepper and half the carrot mixture.
Put 3 tablespoons filling near the bottom of each leaf, fold in the sides, and roll up.
Line a pot with spare leaves. Pack in the rolls seam side down.
Mix the tomato sauce, water, remaining carrot mixture and [[1 tsp]] salt. Pour over the rolls.
Cover and simmer on low for 1 hour until the pork reaches 160°F (71°C). Serve with sour cream.
Mix the soft butter, garlic, dill and [[0.25 tsp]] salt. Shape into a log, wrap, and freeze for [[1 hour]] until hard.
Slice each chicken breast to make a pocket, or pound it flat to about half an inch thick between plastic.
Season the chicken with the remaining salt and pepper.
Cut the butter into 4 sticks. Put one in each breast and roll tightly, folding in the sides to seal.
Dip each roll in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs. Repeat egg and crumbs for a double coat.
Chill the rolls for [[30 minutes]].
Heat the oil to 340°F (170°C). Fry the rolls for 6 minutes, turning, until deep golden.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 12 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C). Rest 5 minutes.
Grate the potatoes and onion with a box grater into a bowl.
Squeeze the mixture in a clean towel to remove as much liquid as you can.
Stir in the egg, flour, salt and pepper.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Spoon 3 tablespoons of batter per pancake into the pan and flatten slightly.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side until crisp and deep golden. Add more oil as needed.
Drain the pancakes on paper towels.
Serve hot with sour cream.
Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a large bowl.
Add the warm milk, egg and [[2 tbsp]] melted butter. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth.
Cover and let rise for [[1 hour]] until doubled.
Divide into 20 balls and place on a greased tray. Let rise for [[30 minutes]].
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Brush the tops with oil.
Bake for 18 minutes until golden brown.
Mix the garlic, dill, [[2 tbsp]] melted butter and a pinch of salt with [[2 tbsp]] water.
Brush the warm buns with the garlic mix. Serve with borscht.
If the cheese is wet, press it in a towel to remove extra liquid.
Mash the cheese with the egg, sugar, vanilla, salt and flour into a thick dough.
Flour your hands and the counter. Shape the dough into 8 patties about half an inch thick.
Dust each patty in flour.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Fry the syrniki for 3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Drain the syrniki on a paper towel.
Serve warm with sour cream.
Cut the fatback into pieces about 2 inches thick. Pat dry with paper towels.
Mix the salt, [[1 tbsp]] pepper and bay leaves.
Rub the salt mix into the pieces on all sides, plus half the garlic.
Layer the fat in a container, skin side down, with garlic between layers.
Cover and keep in the fridge, turning every few hours, for at least 10 hours, then continue turning daily for up to 3 days total. The salt cure is what makes it safe to eat.
Wipe off the extra salt and wrap tightly. Chill until very firm.
Slice the salo into thin strips.
Serve on rye bread with raw garlic.
Heat the oven to 300°F (150°C). Draw three 8-inch circles on parchment and place on trays.
Whip the egg whites with the cream of tartar to soft peaks. Add [[1 cup]] sugar a spoonful at a time and whip to stiff glossy peaks.
Fold in the hazelnuts and flour gently.
Spread the meringue into the circles. Bake for 1 hour 15 minutes until dry and lightly golden. Cool completely.
Whisk the yolks with [[0.5 cup]] sugar in a bowl over simmering water for 8 minutes until thick. Cool.
Beat the butter until fluffy. Add the cooled yolk mix, condensed milk and vanilla, beating to a smooth cream.
Take out half the cream and mix in the cocoa for the topping.
Layer meringue and plain cream, then spread the cocoa cream on top. Chill for [[4 hours]].
Rinse all dried fruit well under cold running water and soak for 15 minutes to remove dust and bitterness.
Put the fruit and [[8 cup]] fresh water in a large pot. Bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to low, add the cinnamon stick and simmer gently for 20 minutes until the fruit is soft and the water is deep amber.
Turn off the heat. Cover and steep for at least 30 minutes so the flavors deepen.
Stir in [[3 tbsp]] honey once the drink has cooled slightly, so the honey keeps its aroma. Serve warm or chilled with some of the fruit in each glass.
nt: Simmered gently, then steeped off the heat
Best swap: use sugar or maple syrup at the same amount in place of honey; swap in dried cherries for the apricots.

st: Rinse the wheat berries well. Put them in a pot with the water and the pinch of salt.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 1 to 1.5 hours until the grains are tender and have split open. Add hot water if the pot runs dry. Drain any extra liquid.
Meanwhile, cover the poppy seeds with boiling water and soak 30 minutes. Drain through a fine sieve.
Grind the drained poppy seeds in a mortar or blender until they turn milky and paste-like. This releases the flavor.
Soak the raisins in hot water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Stir the warm wheat with the ground poppy seeds, honey, raisins and half the walnuts.
Serve warm or cool in a bowl, topped with the remaining walnuts. Add a spoonful of warm water if it feels dry.
nt: Simmered grains, mixed with ground poppy seeds and honey
Best swap: use pearl barley or short grain rice at the same amount if wheat berries are hard to find.

st: Shred the cabbage thin. Place it in a large bowl with [[1.5 tbsp]] salt and massage with clean hands for 5 minutes until it gets juicy and limp.
Stir in the carrot, garlic, peppercorns, caraway and bay leaves until evenly distributed.
Pack the cabbage mix and the beet sticks into a clean jar in layers, pressing down hard with your fist to release juices.
Juices should rise above the vegetables. If not, add a little brine made with [[1 tsp]] salt per [[1 cup]] water.
Weigh the cabbage under its brine with a small plate or clean jar of water. Cover loosely with a cloth.
Ferment at room temperature for 3 to 5 days, pressing down daily and poking with a clean skewer to release gas.
When tangy and bright pink, refrigerate. Serve with potatoes, sausages or borscht. The brine is also drunk as a tonic.
nt: Salt massaged and lacto-fermented, don't cook; 3 to 5 days
Best swap: red cabbage for green and skip the beets, or add 1 apple, grated, for a sweeter sauerkraut.
